messages:
maria: Quick sync — calibration-protocol-v2 produced a surprising perf regression on the FP8->INT8 rollout in nightly runs. p50 token latency up ~12% and p95 spiked on long seqs. Thinking this is tied to our calibration dataset containing heavy outliers + per-channel scaling overhead. ping @kevin @anya
kevin: Can you paste the perf snapshot and the calib sampling procedure you used? length distribution matters a lot — was this run on the same batching settings?
anya: I ran the same config as before (continuous batching ON, KV caching enabled, adaptive_batch_size=8). The only change was switching to per-channel quant stats and adding 10k examples drawn from prod logs without deduping outlier tails.
liam: That deduping bit could be the culprit. If there are many rare long sequences (e.g., code blocks) we skew scales and clamp thresholds, forcing kernels to select fallback accumulation paths.
perf-bot: Profiling summary (last job):

```
model: redwood/gptx-20b
run_id: nightly-2026-03-17
config: fp8->int8 calibration (per-channel), batch_policy: adaptive, kv_cache: enabled
latency p50: 38ms -> 42.6ms (+12.1%)
latency p95: 120ms -> 185ms (+54%)
tokens/sec (hosted): 520 -> 460
kernel mode switches: 11% of requests hit "mixed_accum_fallback"
heavy_reduction_time: +28% (per-channel scales compute)
```

maria: Thanks. So two orthogonal issues: (1) dataset selection with outliers inflates quant scales; (2) per-channel reductions add CPU/GPU reduction overhead and cause kernel mode fallback in our scheduler for hetero shapes. We need a short-term mitigation and a long-term policy.
kevin: Short term: cap per-channel extremes by using percentile clipping (e.g., 99.5/99.9) during stats collection and dedupe contiguous long sequences. That should reduce outlier effect without switching to per-tensor. Also try caching precomputed scales to avoid recompute on warm paths.
anya: Agreed. I can run a quick A/B: current vs clip-99.5 vs per-tensor on a 5k sample. Would also like to test per-channel but quantized with fused reduction kernel (if we can prioritize that kernel in selection).
liam: Per-tensor is ~1.6x faster on our kernels but loses head-level accuracy on cross-attention layers in some tasks. We should validate quality delta on our eval set (QA + summarization).
maria: Long-term: update calibration protocol to mandate stratified sampling across sequence length, token frequency buckets, and remove top 0.2% amplitude outliers. Also experiment with hybrid approach: per-tensor for embedding & feedforward, per-channel for attention weights.
kevin: Note: batching heuristics interact — if adaptive batching upsizes due to lower avg seq we might hide some perf regressions. We should pin batch policy for experiments.
liam: Also watch KV cache behavior: warm vs cold cache changes activation shapes and can trigger different kernels. When we profiled, the majority of p95 cases were cache-warm requests with long prefixes, causing large KV reductions at attention time.
anya: Plan: I will run 3 experiments (pinned batch=8, adaptive off): 1) per-channel with 10k raw prod sample (baseline), 2) per-channel + clip 99.5 + dedupe, 3) per-tensor stratified 10k. I'll push logs and diffs to the perf dashboard.
maria: Please include the microprofile traces for kernel selection and a breakdown of time in: compute_scales, reduction_kernels, matmul_kernels, kv_copy. That will help engineering prioritize fused reduction kernel work.
kevin: If experiment 2 recovers latency to within 2% of baseline and quality delta <0.5 ROUGE on eval, we can adopt clip-99.5 as emergency policy. Otherwise we iterate.
liam: FYI I opened a small PR that adds percentile clipping to the calib tool: tools/calib/percentile_clip.py — basic impl, CPU/GPU paths. I put it under a feature flag.
anya: Nice. I'll run against nightly tomorrow and share numeric diffs. If we still see mode switches, we may need kernel work: reduce atomic reductions or add a fused per-channel reduction kernel to avoid fallback.
maria: Thanks team. Next steps: anya runs experiments, liam stands by for kernel profiling, kevin compiles quality evals. We'll reconvene after results. :thumbsup:
